drugs.moa: Replaces or supplements insulin to move glucose into cells and lower blood sugar.
drugs.route: SC, IV (only regular can go IV)
nursing: Onset ~30 min, peak 2–4 hr — watch for hypoglycemia at the peak
Only regular insulin may be given IV
When mixing, draw up regular (clear) before NPH (cloudy)
teaching: Recognize hypoglycemia: shaky, sweaty, confused → 15 g fast carbs
Eat after dosing to match the peak
drugs.tip: Regular insulin: peak 2–4 hr (hypoglycemia risk), ONLY insulin given IV. Clear before cloudy when mixing.
drugs.pearl: **"Clear before cloudy."** Regular (clear) is drawn up first; only regular goes IV.

drugs.moa: Provides a longer, intermediate duration of glucose control.
nursing: Cloudy suspension — gently roll to mix, never shake
Peak 4–12 hr — teach the client when hypoglycemia is most likely
teaching: Gently roll the vial to mix
drugs.tip: NPH is cloudy, SC only, peaks 4–12 hr. Roll to mix, never shake. Never IV.

drugs.moa: Decreases glucose production by the liver and improves insulin sensitivity — does not cause hypoglycemia alone.
nursing: Hold before and 48 hr after iodinated IV contrast (lactic acidosis risk)
Take with meals to reduce GI upset
teaching: Hold around contrast dye/imaging as instructed
Report muscle pain, trouble breathing, or unusual fatigue
drugs.tip: Metformin: hold before/after IV contrast (lactic acidosis). Take with food. No hypoglycemia on its own.
drugs.pearl: **Hold metformin around contrast dye** — lactic acidosis risk.

drugs.moa: Replaces thyroid hormone (T4) in hypothyroidism, restoring normal metabolism.
adverse: Signs of hyperthyroidism if overdosed (palpitations, weight loss, insomnia)
nursing: Give in the morning on an empty stomach
teaching: Take on an empty stomach, same time each morning
drugs.tip: Levothyroxine: morning, empty stomach, lifelong. Overdose = hyperthyroid signs (palpitations, weight loss).

drugs.moa: Suppresses inflammation and the immune response.
nursing: Monitor blood glucose and for infection
teaching: Do not stop suddenly — taper as directed
drugs.tip: Steroids: taper (never stop abruptly → adrenal crisis), raise glucose, mask/increase infection, take with food.
drugs.pearl: **Steroids = Sugar up, Susceptible to infection, Swelling, Slow tapering.**
